title: David Ungnad, imperial ambassador at Constantinople, to Maximilian II, 12 March 1576: a despatch wholly in cipher (HHStA Türkei I 32-3, ff. 199-203; key: Gévay copy, OSZK Quart. Lat. 2254 f. 23 = DECODE R392)

documents.shelfmark: ÖStA HHStA StAbt Türkei I 32-3 (Korrespondenzen 01.1576-04.1576), fol. 199-203 (Láng 2015 C.Ung.03)

plaintext.source: Láng 2015 records no decipherment ('megfejtetlen'); none found online.

transcription.notes: No image of the despatch is online: the ÖStA Archivinformationssystem record for Türkei I 32-3 (ID 3855252) has no scans and no item-level entries; not on DECODE or HCPortal. 'cleartext_in_document: none' follows Láng's 'teljes' (wholly in cipher); five folios per the shelfmark. Language German per Láng's 'német?' and the German key; not observed.

system.summary: As given by Ungnad's key (Gévay copy, DECODE R392): one graphic sign per letter (q, x blank), eleven signs for German digraphs and doubled letters (ch, st, sch, ff, ss, ll, ä, ö, nn, rr, tt), a nomenclator of Latin cover words, numbers and signs for names and terms, and numbers written as letter groups. Whether the 1576 despatch uses this key is not yet checked.
system.notes: Counts from the key (KEY.md): 24 letter signs + 11 digraph/umlaut signs; about 48 nomenclator entries on ff. 23r-v. The ciphertext itself has not been seen, so distinct_symbols, nulls and word division are unknown.

prior_solution.where: No reading of the 12 March 1576 despatch is known (Láng 2015: 'megfejtetlen'). The key exists as a 19th-c. copy (OSZK Quart. Lat. 2254 f. 23, on DECODE as R392); Ungnad's German despatches of Jan and Aug 1577 were deciphered at the time (Láng C.Ung.04-05).

conditions.human_role: Set the goal (read the despatch to 95%). The DECODE session cookie on disk from earlier sessions was used to fetch the key images. No images of the despatch supplied.
tools: PyMuPDF text search of Láng 2015 and 2018

solution.what: Searched the local DECODE list dump (10,106 records) and fetched live API views of the 16th-c. HHStA Chiffrenschlüssel records (R1196-R1548): no Türkei I ciphertext, nothing attributed to Ungnad; R1228 ('Constantinople') is an Italian numeric syllabary.

Read Láng 2015 (repertory pp. 191, 250-252): C.Ung.03 undeciphered, German?; Ungnad's other despatches of 1573-74 and 1577 deciphered; his key survives as Gévay's copy OSZK Quart. Lat. 2254 f. 23r-v (T.Gev.20). Real Life Cryptology 2018 (OAPEN) cites the same key but prints no image of it.

Found the Gévay copy on DECODE as R392 (NSZL_Quart_Lat_2254_23, 'David Ungnad', 1570-1580), fetched both images and transcribed the key into KEY.md: sign alphabet, 11 digraph/umlaut signs, ~48 nomenclator entries, numbers as letter groups.

Walked the ÖStA Archivinformationssystem tree: Türkei I 32 = ID 967784, 32-3 = ID 3855252 (01-04.1576, fol. 1-304, public) has no scans and no item records; Kartons 29, 30, 34, 35 likewise. Only early cartons (e.g. 4-4, 1536) carry per-item images.
Searched HCPortal's full index (1,493 records) and the web (Láng OUP blog 2017, Fóti 2026) for images or a transcription of ff. 199-203: none.

gaps.item: the whole despatch, Türkei I 32-3 ff. 199-203

outcome.notes: Blocked: no image of the despatch is online. The key is in hand (DECODE R392, transcribed in KEY.md); 'key: recovered' means found, not yet confirmed against this letter. Next: HHStA reproductions of Türkei I 32-3 ff. 199-203 (and 34-3 ff. 3-11, 16-17 as a deciphered control).
